```text
const _debugRenderer = (
  canvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
  appState: AppState,
  elements: readonly OrderedExcalidrawElement[],
  scale: number,
) => {
  const [normalizedWidth, normalizedHeight] = getNormalizedCanvasDimensions(
    canvas,
    scale,
  );

  const context = bootstrapCanvas({
    canvas,
    scale,
    normalizedWidth,
    normalizedHeight,
    viewBackgroundColor: "transparent",
  });

  // Apply zoom
  context.save();
  context.translate(
    appState.scrollX * appState.zoom.value,
    appState.scrollY * appState.zoom.value,
  );

  renderOrigin(context, appState.zoom.value);
  renderBindings(context, elements, appState.zoom.value);

  if (
    window.visualDebug?.currentFrame &&
    window.visualDebug?.data &&
    window.visualDebug.data.length > 0
  ) {
    // Render only one frame
    const [idx] = debugFrameData();

    render(window.visualDebug.data[idx], context, appState);
  } else {
    // Render all debug frames
    window.visualDebug?.data.forEach((frame) => {
      render(frame, context, appState);
    });
  }

  if (window.visualDebug) {
    window.visualDebug!.data =
      window.visualDebug?.data.map((frame) =>
        frame.filter((el) => el.permanent),
      ) ?? [];
  }
};

const debugFrameData = (): [number, number] => {
  const currentFrame = window.visualDebug?.currentFrame ?? 0;
  const frameCount = window.visualDebug?.data.length ?? 0;

  if (frameCount > 0) {
    return [currentFrame % frameCount, window.visualDebug?.currentFrame ?? 0];
  }

  return [0, 0];
};
```

```text
const renderBindings = (
  context: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  elements: readonly OrderedExcalidrawElement[],
  zoom: number,
) => {
  const elementsMap = arrayToMap(elements);
  const dim = 16;
  elements.forEach((element) => {
    if (element.isDeleted) {
      return;
    }

    if (isArrowElement(element)) {
      if (element.startBinding) {
        if (
          !elementsMap
            .get(element.startBinding.elementId)
            ?.boundElements?.find((e) => e.id === element.id)
        ) {
          return;
        }

        _renderBinding(
          context,
          element.startBinding,
          elementsMap,
          zoom,
          dim,
          dim,
          element.startBinding?.mode === "orbit" ? "red" : "black",
        );
      }

      if (element.endBinding) {
        if (
          !elementsMap
            .get(element.endBinding.elementId)
            ?.boundElements?.find((e) => e.id === element.id)
        ) {
          return;
        }
        _renderBinding(
          context,
          element.endBinding,
          elementsMap,
          zoom,
          dim,
          dim,
          element.endBinding?.mode === "orbit" ? "red" : "black",
        );
      }
    }

    if (isBindableElement(element) && element.boundElements?.length) {
      element.boundElements.forEach((boundElement) => {
        if (boundElement.type !== "arrow") {
          return;
        }

        const arrow = elementsMap.get(
          boundElement.id,
        ) as ExcalidrawArrowElement;

        if (arrow && arrow.startBinding?.elementId === element.id) {
          _renderBindableBinding(
            arrow.startBinding,
            context,
            elementsMap,
            zoom,
            dim,
            dim,
            "green",
          );
        }
        if (arrow && arrow.endBinding?.elementId === element.id) {
          _renderBindableBinding(
            arrow.endBinding,
            context,
            elementsMap,
            zoom,
            dim,
            dim,
            "green",
          );
        }
      });
    }
  });
};
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 00:08:59Z)**_

## What the red and green loops are

They come from Excalidraw's **Visual Debug** overlay, a tool for developers that only exists in dev builds. It's not part of normal rendering.

| Piece | Location | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On/off switch | [excalidraw-app/components/AppMainMenu.tsx:61-76](excalidraw-app/components/AppMainMenu.tsx#L61-L76) | The **"Visual Debug"** item in the ☰ main menu. It only appears when `isDevEnv()` is true, and it saves your choice in `localStorage["excalidraw-debug"]` |
| The overlay | [excalidraw-app/components/DebugCanvas.tsx](excalidraw-app/components/DebugCanvas.tsx) | A separate `<canvas>` placed over the editor ([App.tsx:1259](excalidraw-app/App.tsx#L1259)) |
| What it draws | [DebugCanvas.tsx:210-300](excalidraw-app/components/DebugCanvas.tsx#L210-L300), `renderBindings` | For every bound arrow, it marks the binding at **the arrow's end** (red if the binding is in `"orbit"` mode, black otherwise) and at **the shape's end** (green) |
| When it redraws | [excalidraw-app/App.tsx:725-732](excalidraw-app/App.tsx#L725-L732) | On every `onChange`, using **all scene elements** |

That's why the loops appear as soon as an arrow binds to a shape and disappear when it unbinds: the overlay is drawing the binding data itself. You must have turned on Visual Debug at some point, and since the setting is saved, it stays on after reloads.

## Why it was hard to find

1. **It's in the wrong half of the repo for where I was looking.** All normal drawing happens in `packages/excalidraw/renderer/` and `packages/element/`, so I searched there first. This overlay lives in **`excalidraw-app/`**, the host app, outside the library entirely.
2. **The colours are written as words.** The code uses `"red"`, `"green"` and `"black"`, while the rest of the renderer uses hex or `rgba(...)`. My first searches looked for hex and rgba values and missed it. A search for the plain words is what turned it up.
3. **It skips the renderer completely.** It doesn't go through `Renderer.getRenderableElements` or `InteractiveCanvas`. It receives the raw `elements` from `onChange` and draws on its own canvas. That's also **why my filter doesn't affect it**: it's another separate rendering path, like embeddables and frame names were.
4. **It's hidden in normal use.** It only exists in dev mode, it's off by default, and it's turned on from a menu item that's easy to forget about.

## Should it respect hiding?

**This isn't a bug users would ever see.** The overlay isn't included in production builds, and real users never see it. So there are two reasonable approaches:

- **A. Leave it unfiltered (my recommendation).** It's a diagnostic tool that's meant to show **the real scene data**, and that's actually useful for this feature. While Bob is hidden, the overlay still shows his bindings, which shows that hiding didn't touch or remove anything.
- **B. Filter it as well.** That's a one-line change in [excalidraw-app/App.tsx:727](excalidraw-app/App.tsx#L727), passing only visible elements to `debugRenderer`. It keeps testing less confusing, but it hides exactly the information the tool exists to show.

If you'd rather not see it while testing, just turn it off: ☰ menu → **Visual Debug**.

Nothing has changed since the frame-name fix. Tell me A or B, and type **"Approved"** when you're ready for step 2.

All of these are Excalidraw core maintainers, and every commit links to an upstream PR number. I checked the full history of [DebugCanvas.tsx](excalidraw-app/components/DebugCanvas.tsx) and [visualdebug.ts](packages/element/src/visualdebug.ts), plus `git blame` on the menu item and on the `debugRenderer` call. None of the commits are by your team (Cashen Croft, AntWill-08, NotaThomas, tristanraab or tuna-fisher). The tool was already part of the codebase you forked.

### It doesn't break the architecture either

Bypassing the renderer is a deliberate choice here:

- **It's meant to show raw data.** A debug overlay exists to show what's actually stored, such as the binding records, not what the renderer chose to draw. Routing it through `Renderer` would hide exactly what it's there to show.
- **It sits in the app layer on purpose.** It's in `excalidraw-app/`, gated by `isDevEnv()`, and never included in the npm library or the production build.
- **It only reads.** It never changes the scene.

So there's nothing to report about a peer, and we'll leave it as it is (option A). The only thing to note for your design doc is that **dev-only tools show unfiltered scene data**. That's expected, and it's handy for checking that hiding never changes the data.

```text
    x: number,

      | {
          includeBoundTextElement?: boolean;
```

```text
export const getHoveredElementForBinding = (
  point: Readonly<GlobalPoint>,
  elements: readonly Ordered<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>[],
  elementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  tolerance?: number,
): NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement> | null => {
  const candidateElements = getAllHoveredElementAtPoint(
    point,
    elements,
    elementsMap,
    tolerance,
  );

  if (!candidateElements || candidateElements.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  if (candidateElements.length === 1) {
    return candidateElements[0];
  }

  // Prefer smaller shapes
  return candidateElements
    .sort(
      (a, b) => b.width ** 2 + b.height ** 2 - (a.width ** 2 + a.height ** 2),
    )
    .pop() as NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>;
};

export const getHoveredElementForFocusPoint = (
  point: GlobalPoint,
  arrow: ExcalidrawArrowElement,
  elements: readonly Ordered<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>[],
  elementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  tolerance?: number,
): NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement> | null => {
  const candidateElements: NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>[] = [];
  // We need to to hit testing from front (end of the array) to back (beginning of the array)
  // because array is ordered from lower z-index to highest and we want element z-index
  // with higher z-index
  for (let index = elements.length - 1; index >= 0; --index) {
    const element = elements[index];

    invariant(
      !element.isDeleted,
      "Elements in the function parameter for getAllElementsAtPositionForBinding() should not contain deleted elements",
    );

    if (
      isBindableElement(element, false) &&
      bindingBorderTest(element, point, elementsMap, tolerance)
    ) {
      candidateElements.push(element);
    }
  }

  if (!candidateElements || candidateElements.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  if (candidateElements.length === 1) {
    return candidateElements[0];
  }
```

```text
function prepareDataForJSONExport(
  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
  appState: AppState,
  files: BinaryFiles,
  app: AppClassProperties,
): { abortController: AbortController; data: Promise<JSONExportData> } {
  const abortController = new AbortController();
  const signal = abortController.signal;

  const dataPromise = new Promise<JSONExportData>(async (resolve) => {
    try {
      if (app.props.onExport) {
        await handleOnExportResult(
          app.props.onExport(
            "json",
            {
              elements,
              appState,
              files,
            },
            {
              signal,
            },
          ),
          {
            app,
            signal,
          },
        );
      }
    } catch (error: any) {
      if (error?.name === "AbortError") {
        // if abort error, assume it's a reaction on the signal being aborted
        console.warn(
          `onExport() aborted by host app (signal aborted: ${signal.aborted})`,
        );
      } else {
        // non-abort error
        //
        console.error("Error during props.onExport() handling", error);
      }

      // either way, we currently don't allow host apps to cancel save actions
      // so we resolve to orig data
    }

    resolve({
      elements,
      appState,
      // return latest files in case they finished loading during onExport
      files: app.files,
    });
  });

  return {
    abortController,
    data: dataPromise,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Save actions
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```typescript
import { arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";
import { getElementCreatorId, getElementsInGroup } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ElementsMap, ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import type { AppState } from "../types";

export type LocalVisibilityState = Pick<AppState, "hiddenCollaboratorIds">;

/**
 * Whether the element is hidden on this client by the collaborator
 * visibility controls. Purely a local view filter — scene data is untouched.
 */
export const isElementHiddenLocally = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
  { hiddenCollaboratorIds }: LocalVisibilityState,
): boolean => {
  if (!hiddenCollaboratorIds.size) {
    return false;
  }
  return hiddenCollaboratorIds.has(getElementCreatorId(element, elementsMap));
};

/**
 * Returns only the elements visible on this client (e.g. for export).
 * Returns the input array as-is when nothing is hidden.
 *
 * @param elementsMap used to resolve bound text containers. Defaults to
 * a map of `elements`, so pass the full scene map when `elements` is a subset.
 */
export const getLocallyVisibleElements = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  appState: LocalVisibilityState,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap = arrayToMap(elements),
): readonly T[] => {
  if (!appState.hiddenCollaboratorIds.size) {
    return elements;
  }
  return elements.filter(
    (element) => !isElementHiddenLocally(element, elementsMap, appState),
  );
};

/**
 * Selection safety net: hidden elements must never stay selected, otherwise
 * actions (delete, ungroup, move…) would modify them for every collaborator.
 *
 * Returns the selection-related appState to apply, or `null` if the
 * selection contains no hidden elements.
 */
export const getSelectionWithoutHiddenElements = (
  appState: LocalVisibilityState &
    Pick<
      AppState,
      "selectedElementIds" | "selectedGroupIds" | "selectedLinearElement"
    >,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): Pick<
  AppState,
  "selectedElementIds" | "selectedGroupIds" | "selectedLinearElement"
> | null => {
  if (!appState.hiddenCollaboratorIds.size) {
    return null;
  }

  const isHidden = (id: string) => {
    const element = elementsMap.get(id);
    return !!element && isElementHiddenLocally(element, elementsMap, appState);
  };

  const hiddenSelectedIds = Object.keys(appState.selectedElementIds).filter(
    isHidden,
  );
  // a group containing hidden members can't stay selected as a group, or
  // group actions (ungroup, group bbox…) would reach the hidden members
  const groupIdsWithHiddenMembers = Object.keys(
    appState.selectedGroupIds,
  ).filter((groupId) =>
    getElementsInGroup(elementsMap, groupId).some((el) => isHidden(el.id)),
  );
  const isLinearElementHidden =
    !!appState.selectedLinearElement &&
    isHidden(appState.selectedLinearElement.elementId);

  if (
    !hiddenSelectedIds.length &&
    !groupIdsWithHiddenMembers.length &&
    !isLinearElementHidden
  ) {
    return null;
  }

  const selectedElementIds = { ...appState.selectedElementIds };
  for (const id of hiddenSelectedIds) {
    delete selectedElementIds[id];
  }

  const selectedGroupIds = { ...appState.selectedGroupIds };
  for (const groupId of groupIdsWithHiddenMembers) {
    delete selectedGroupIds[groupId];
  }

  return {
    selectedElementIds,
    selectedGroupIds,
    selectedLinearElement: isLinearElementHidden
      ? null
      : appState.selectedLinearElement,
  };
};
```

```text
  private getTextBindableContainerAtPosition(x: number, y: number) {
    const elements = this.scene.getNonDeletedElements();
    const selectedElements = this.scene.getSelectedElements(this.state);
    if (selectedElements.length === 1) {
      return isTextBindableContainer(selectedElements[0], false)
        ? selectedElements[0]
        : null;
    }
    let hitElement = null;
    // We need to do hit testing from front (end of the array) to back (beginning of the array)
    for (let index = elements.length - 1; index >= 0; --index) {
      if (elements[index].isDeleted) {
        continue;
      }
      const [x1, y1, x2, y2] = getElementAbsoluteCoords(
        elements[index],
        this.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap(),
      );
      if (
        isArrowElement(elements[index]) &&
        hitElementItself({
          point: pointFrom(x, y),
          element: elements[index],
          elementsMap: this.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap(),
          threshold: this.getElementHitThreshold(elements[index]),
        })
      ) {
        hitElement = elements[index];
        break;
      } else if (x1 < x && x < x2 && y1 < y && y < y2) {
        // to allow binding to containers within frames,
        // ignore frames in hit testing
        if (isFrameLikeElement(elements[index])) {
          continue;
        }

        hitElement = elements[index];
        break;
      }
    }
```

```bash
describe("collaborator visibility (interaction safety)", () => {
  // solid fill so clicking the interior counts as a hit
  const createSolidRect = (id: string, x: number, groupIds: string[] = []) =>
    API.createElement({
      type: "rectangle",
      id,
      x,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
      backgroundColor: "red",
      fillStyle: "solid",
      groupIds,
    });

  const isDeleted = (id: string) =>
    h.elements.find((el) => el.id === id)!.isDeleted;

  const getSelectedIds = () =>
    API.getSelectedElements()
      .map((el) => el.id)
      .sort();

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    API.setElements([
      stamp(createSolidRect("alice-rect", 0), "alice"),
      stamp(createSolidRect("bob-rect", 200), "bob"),
    ]);
  });

  it("clicking a hidden element doesn't select it", () => {
    setHidden(["bob"]);

    mouse.clickAt(250, 50);
    expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual([]);

    mouse.clickAt(50, 50);
    expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);
  });

  it("box-selecting skips hidden elements", () => {
    setHidden(["bob"]);

    mouse.downAt(-50, -50);
    mouse.moveTo(350, 150);
    mouse.upAt(350, 150);

    expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);
  });

  it("select all + delete never deletes hidden elements", () => {
    setHidden(["bob"]);

    Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.A);
    });
    expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);

    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.DELETE);
    expect(isDeleted("alice-rect")).toBe(true);
    expect(isDeleted("bob-rect")).toBe(false);
  });

  it("hiding a selected element deselects it", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([h.elements[0], h.elements[1]]);
    expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect", "bob-rect"]);

    setHidden(["bob"]);
    expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);
  });

  describe("mixed-collaborator groups", () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      API.setElements([
        stamp(createSolidRect("alice-rect", 0, ["group"]), "alice"),
        stamp(createSolidRect("bob-rect", 200, ["group"]), "bob"),
      ]);
    });

    it("selecting a visible member never selects hidden members", () => {
      setHidden(["bob"]);

      mouse.clickAt(50, 50);
      expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);
      expect(h.state.selectedGroupIds).not.toHaveProperty("group");

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.DELETE);
      expect(isDeleted("alice-rect")).toBe(true);
      expect(isDeleted("bob-rect")).toBe(false);
    });

    const eraseThroughAliceRect = () => {
      UI.clickTool("eraser");
      mouse.downAt(-20, 50);
      mouse.moveTo(20, 50);
      mouse.moveTo(60, 50);
      mouse.upAt(60, 50);
    };

    it("(control) erasing a member erases the whole group", () => {
      eraseThroughAliceRect();
      expect(isDeleted("alice-rect")).toBe(true);
      expect(isDeleted("bob-rect")).toBe(true);
    });

    it("erasing a visible member never erases hidden members", () => {
      setHidden(["bob"]);

      eraseThroughAliceRect();
      expect(isDeleted("alice-rect")).toBe(true);
      expect(isDeleted("bob-rect")).toBe(false);
    });
  });
});

describe("collaborator visibility (export)", () => {
  const aliceRect = stamp(createRect("alice-rect", 0), "alice");
  const bobRect = stamp(createRect("bob-rect", 20), "bob");

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw />);
    API.setElements([aliceRect, bobRect]);
  });

  const getExportedIds = (exportSelectionOnly = false) =>
    prepareElementsForExport(h.elements, h.state, exportSelectionOnly)
      .exportedElements.map((el) => el.id)
      .sort();

  it("exports everything when nothing is hidden", () => {
    expect(getExportedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect", "bob-rect"]);
  });

  it("exports only visible elements", () => {
    setHidden(["bob"]);
    expect(getExportedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);
  });

  it("export follows the current visibility", () => {
    setHidden(["bob"]);
    expect(getExportedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);

    setHidden(["alice"]);
    expect(getExportedIds()).toEqual(["bob-rect"]);
  });

  it("getLocallyVisibleElements returns the same array when nothing is hidden", () => {
    const elements = h.elements;
    expect(getLocallyVisibleElements(elements, h.state)).toBe(elements);
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 00:26:30Z)**_

## Step 2 done: interaction safety and visible-only exports

Hidden drawings can no longer be clicked, selected, erased or found by search. Exports now contain only what's visible. The typecheck and lint pass, and the full suite passes: 125 files, 1,855 tests, with no new snapshot changes.

### How it works

```
                  isElementHiddenLocally()   ◄── same single check as step 1
                            │
      ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
      ▼                     ▼                         ▼                      ▼
 HIT-TESTING           SAFETY NET                 CASCADES               EXPORTS
 getElementsAtPosition componentDidUpdate:        eraser group expansion getLocallyVisibleElements()
  (clicks, hover,      if the selection holds a   skips hidden members    ├ prepareElementsForExport
   double-click, text  hidden element, drop it;                           │  (image dialog, copy as
   edit, click-erase)  drop selected groups that                          │   image, re-saving an image)
 text container pick   have hidden members;                               ├ prepareDataForJSONExport
 frame drop target     clear hidden linear editor                         │  (Save, Save as)
 motion-path target    → covers Select All, group                         ├ LayerUI → JSONExportDialog
 box-select            click, search, lasso, and                          │  (link, Excalidraw+)
 search                anything added later                               └ excalidraw-app: share link,
                                                                             2× Excalidraw+ export
```

**Two layers of protection:**

1. **The direct paths** (clicks, box-select, the eraser) skip hidden elements up front.
2. **The safety net** is in `componentDidUpdate`. Whatever path selects something (Select All, clicking a group member, lasso, search, or code someone adds later), hidden elements are dropped from the selection right after React applies the change. That's always before the next key press, so Delete, Ungroup or Move can never reach a hidden element.

### Files changed in this step

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| [scene/visibility.ts](packages/excalidraw/scene/visibility.ts) | Added `getLocallyVisibleElements()`, which returns the **same array** when nothing is hidden, so there's no cost in that case. Added `getSelectionWithoutHiddenElements()` for the safety net |
| [components/App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx) | The safety net in `componentDidUpdate`, plus filters in `getElementsAtPosition`, `getTextBindableContainerAtPosition`, `getTopLayerFrameAtSceneCoords` (so nothing gets dropped into a hidden frame), the motion-path target scan from #45, and box-select |
| [eraser/index.ts](packages/excalidraw/eraser/index.ts) | Erasing a grouped shape no longer erases the group's hidden members. **This was the one real way to delete another person's drawings** |
| [data/index.ts](packages/excalidraw/data/index.ts) | `prepareElementsForExport` filters when `hiddenCollaboratorIds` is passed. It's optional, so existing callers that don't pass it behave as before |
| [actions/actionExport.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionExport.tsx) | Save and Save as write only visible elements, as do re-saves of an image file with the scene embedded |
| [components/LayerUI.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/LayerUI.tsx) | The JSON export dialog (shareable link, Excalidraw+ panel) receives only visible elements |
| [components/SearchMenu.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/SearchMenu.tsx) | Ctrl+F no longer finds or jumps to hidden text or frames |
| [index.tsx](packages/excalidraw/index.tsx) | Exports `getLocallyVisibleElements` publicly so the host app can use it |
| [excalidraw-app/App.tsx](excalidraw-app/App.tsx) | The shareable link and both Excalidraw+ exports use visible elements only |
| [tests/collaboratorVisibility.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorVisibility.test.tsx) | **12 new tests**: click, box-select, Select All + Delete, deselect on hide, mixed groups (select + delete), eraser, and export. Two **control tests** (one box-select, one eraser) run with nothing hidden, to prove the safety tests actually exercise those code paths |

### Checking it yourself

Use a solo tab and the same console helpers as before (`stamp`, `hide`, `show`). Draw two shapes, then `stamp("alice")` the first and `stamp("bob")` the second. Run `hide("bob")` and try:

| Try | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Click where Bob's shape is | Nothing is selected |
| Drag a selection box over both | Only Alice's shape is selected |
| **Ctrl+A, then Delete** | Only Alice's shape is deleted. Run `hide()` and Bob's shape is still there |
| Select both shapes, group them (Ctrl+G), run `hide("bob")`, then click Alice's shape | Only Alice's shape is selected, with no group box |
| Eraser tool over Alice's shape while the two are grouped | Only Alice's shape is erased |
| Export image (Ctrl+Shift+E) | The preview shows only Alice's shape. Run `hide("alice")`, reopen the dialog, and it shows only Bob's |
| Save to disk, then open the file | It contains only the shapes that were visible |
| Ctrl+F for text inside Bob's shape | No results |

After each test, `show()` should list Bob's element with `isDeleted: false`.

### Two decisions before step 3

**1. Arrows can still bind to hidden shapes.** Drawing an arrow near Bob's hidden shape will snap to it and add the arrow to that shape's `boundElements`. It isn't destructive, but it is confusing, and it does modify the hidden element. Binding reads the scene directly in about 10 places inside `@excalidraw/element` (`binding.ts`, `linearElementEditor.ts`, `elbowArrow.ts`), which doesn't know anything about visibility.

- **A. Defer it (my recommendation)** to the interaction work in parent issue #14, where it belongs, and record it as a known limitation in the PR.
- **B. Fix it now** by giving `Scene` an optional "interactive elements" filter that binding uses. That's a bigger change that touches the element package's API.

**2. Changes that follow from editing visible elements.** Some ordinary edits to _visible_ elements also update related hidden ones, so the scene stays consistent:

- Moving a visible shape reroutes a hidden arrow bound to it.
- Deleting a visible frame **unparents** its hidden children (`frameId: null`). It doesn't delete them, and they don't stay selected.
- I _expect_ that dragging a visible frame also moves the hidden elements inside it, but I haven't tested that.

These edits would happen exactly the same way if those elements were visible, and nothing gets deleted. **Are you OK treating these as acceptable?** Under the rule as implemented, hidden elements are never the **target** of an action, and are never deleted by one.

The dependencies only point **downward**: element package ← scene layer ← App and components ← host app. `@excalidraw/element` doesn't import anything from the editor, and the editor doesn't import anything from `excalidraw-app`. That's the layering Excalidraw expects, and ESLint enforces it (it's what flagged my first ownership test).

## How each part compares with Excalidraw's own patterns

| What I did | Similar code Excalidraw already has | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A view-only AppState field, never saved or synced | `collaborators`, `followedBy` and `userToFollow` use the same `{browser:false, export:false, server:false}` setting | ✅ Follows precedent |
| Skipping hidden elements in `getElementsAtPosition` | The **same function** already skips `locked` elements and bound text with the same `.filter()` chain. Hidden is just another condition there | ✅ Follows precedent closely |
| Filtering in `Renderer.getRenderableElementsMap` | The same function already skips the element being edited and the new element | ✅ Follows precedent |
| Separate filters for DOM-rendered items (embeddables, frame names) | Both functions already do their own viewport culling (`isElementInViewport`) | ✅ Follows precedent |
| A pure helper in `@excalidraw/element` (`ownership.ts`) | `typeChecks.ts`, `groups.ts`, `textElement.ts`: data-only helpers that take elements and know nothing about AppState | ✅ Follows precedent |
| A filter in the data layer (`prepareElementsForExport`) | The same function already decides _which_ elements to export (selection only, frame contents) | ✅ Follows precedent |
| The host app calling a public helper | excalidraw-app already imports `reconcileElements`, `CaptureUpdateAction` and others from the public API | ✅ Follows precedent |
| **A fix-up `setState` in `componentDidUpdate`** | Some precedent exists in the same method (`exportWithDarkMode`, `showWelcomeScreen`), but **upstream never uses this pattern for selection** | ⚠️ Deliberate departure |

## The weak spots, honestly

**1. The safety net in `componentDidUpdate` (the main concern).**

- **The usual Excalidraw approach:** state should be correct _at the point it's set_. Handlers and actions compute the right selection and return it, and nothing fixes it up afterwards.
- **Why I departed from it:** there are more than 20 places where selection changes (`selectGroupsForSelectedElements` alone is called in about 12 of them, plus `actionSelectAll`, lasso and search). Filtering each one individually is easy to get wrong, and the cost of missing one is deleting someone else's drawing.
- **The cost:** when a hidden element does get selected, there's one extra render. There's no extra render in the normal case, because `getSelectionWithoutHiddenElements` returns `null`.
- **A version closer to Excalidraw's style:** put the filter in the **two chokepoints** that most selection changes go through, `selectGroupsForSelectedElements` and `makeNextSelectedElementIds`, and keep the `componentDidUpdate` net only as a backup. I can make that change if you'd like it closer to upstream. It's a bit more work, and it doesn't improve safety.

**2. `ownership.ts` sits in the element package.** It's a pure data accessor, so it fits there. The catch is that the `customData.creatorId` convention is effectively a **collaboration feature** living in a package meant to be general-purpose. The alternative is to move it to `packages/excalidraw/scene/`. The cost of that is that `eraser` and other element-level code couldn't use it in future without importing from the editor package, which ESLint forbids. I'd keep it where it is.

**3. Filters are spread across several places.** There are 12 call sites rather than one filter. That's inherent: Excalidraw has no single list of "interactive elements". Every call site uses the **same single check**, so the _rule_ lives in one place, but someone adding a new hit-test in future would have to remember to call it. A short comment in `visibility.ts` listing the call sites would help with that.

**4. Not done through the ActionManager yet.** So far the state is only set from the console. Steps 5 and 6 add the actions (`toggleCollaboratorVisibility` and the others), which is the normal Excalidraw path for UI → state. That gap is temporary.

## My recommendation

The architecture is sound and mostly follows existing patterns. The one place it departs from upstream style is the `componentDidUpdate` safety net. If this PR needs to look upstream-quality for your course, I'd add the two chokepoint filters in step 2.5 and keep the net as a backup. Otherwise, leave it as it is.

Three things are still open: whether to add the chokepoint filters, decision 1 (arrow binding to hidden shapes: **A**, defer, or **B**, fix now), and decision 2 (whether non-destructive changes that follow from editing visible elements are acceptable). Type **"Approved"** with your answers to continue.

```text
export const makeNextSelectedElementIds = (
  nextSelectedElementIds: AppState["selectedElementIds"],
  prevState: Pick<AppState, "selectedElementIds">,
) => {
  if (isShallowEqual(prevState.selectedElementIds, nextSelectedElementIds)) {
    return prevState.selectedElementIds;
  }

  return nextSelectedElementIds;
};
```

```text
export const getAllHoveredElementAtPoint = (
  point: Readonly<GlobalPoint>,
  elements: readonly Ordered<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>[],
  elementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  tolerance?: number,
): NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>[] => {
  const candidateElements: NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>[] = [];
  // We need to to hit testing from front (end of the array) to back (beginning of the array)
  // because array is ordered from lower z-index to highest and we want element z-index
  // with higher z-index
  for (let index = elements.length - 1; index >= 0; --index) {
    const element = elements[index];

    invariant(
      !element.isDeleted,
      "Elements in the function parameter for getAllElementsAtPositionForBinding() should not contain deleted elements",
    );

    if (
      isBindableElement(element, false) &&
      bindingBorderTest(element, point, elementsMap, tolerance)
    ) {
      candidateElements.push(element);

      if (
        hasBackground(element.type) &&
        !isTransparent(element.backgroundColor)
      ) {
        break;
      }
    }
  }

  return candidateElements;
};
```

```text
const updateArrowBindings = (
  latestElement: NonDeleted<ExcalidrawArrowElement>,
  startOrEnd: "startBinding" | "endBinding",
  elementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  scene: Scene,
  appState: AppState,
) => {
  invariant(
    !isElbowArrow(latestElement),
    "Elbow arrows not supported for indirect updates",
  );

  const binding = latestElement[startOrEnd];

    binding &&
    (elementsMap.get(
      binding.elementId,
    ) as NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>);

    latestElement,

        scene,

  }
```

```bash
describe("collaborator visibility (chokepoints)", () => {
  // solid fill so pointer hits/bindings work on the interior
  const createSolidRect = (id: string, x: number, groupIds: string[] = []) =>
    API.createElement({
      type: "rectangle",
      id,
      x,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
      backgroundColor: "red",
      fillStyle: "solid",
      groupIds,
    });

  const getArrow = () =>
    h.elements.find(
      (el): el is ExcalidrawArrowElement => el.type === "arrow" && !el.isDeleted,
    )!;

  const drawArrowFromAliceToBob = () => {
    UI.clickTool("arrow");
    mouse.downAt(50, 50);
    mouse.moveTo(200, 50);
    mouse.moveTo(350, 50);
    mouse.upAt(350, 50);
  };

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    API.setElements([
      stamp(createSolidRect("alice-rect", 0), "alice"),
      stamp(createSolidRect("bob-rect", 300), "bob"),
    ]);
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    mouse.reset();
  });

  describe("selection (selectGroupsForSelectedElements)", () => {
    it("never returns hidden elements, even without the App safety net", () => {
      API.setElements([
        stamp(createSolidRect("alice-rect", 0, ["group"]), "alice"),
        stamp(createSolidRect("bob-rect", 300, ["group"]), "bob"),
      ]);
      setHidden(["bob"]);

      const result = selectGroupsForSelectedElements(
        {
          selectedElementIds: { "alice-rect": true, "bob-rect": true },
          editingGroupId: null,
        },
        h.app.scene.getNonDeletedElements(),
        h.state,
        null,
      );

      expect(Object.keys(result.selectedElementIds)).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);
      // with its hidden member excluded the group has a single member, so it
      // isn't selected as a group
      expect(result.selectedGroupIds.group).toBeFalsy();
    });

    it("(control) selects the whole group when nothing is hidden", () => {
      API.setElements([
        stamp(createSolidRect("alice-rect", 0, ["group"]), "alice"),
        stamp(createSolidRect("bob-rect", 300, ["group"]), "bob"),
      ]);

      const result = selectGroupsForSelectedElements(
        { selectedElementIds: { "alice-rect": true }, editingGroupId: null },
        h.app.scene.getNonDeletedElements(),
        h.state,
        null,
      );

      expect(Object.keys(result.selectedElementIds).sort()).toEqual([
        "alice-rect",
        "bob-rect",
      ]);
      expect(result.selectedGroupIds.group).toBe(true);
    });
  });

  describe("arrow binding", () => {
    it("(control) a new arrow binds to both shapes", () => {
      drawArrowFromAliceToBob();

      expect(getArrow().startBinding?.elementId).toBe("alice-rect");
      expect(getArrow().endBinding?.elementId).toBe("bob-rect");
    });

    it("a new arrow can't bind to a hidden shape", () => {
      setHidden(["bob"]);
      drawArrowFromAliceToBob();

      expect(getArrow().startBinding?.elementId).toBe("alice-rect");
      expect(getArrow().endBinding).toBeNull();
      // and the hidden shape's data is untouched
      expect(
        h.elements.find((el) => el.id === "bob-rect")!.boundElements ?? [],
      ).toEqual([]);
    });

    it("existing bindings to a hidden shape are kept", () => {
      drawArrowFromAliceToBob();
      expect(getArrow().endBinding?.elementId).toBe("bob-rect");

      setHidden(["bob"]);

      // move the visible, bound shape
      UI.clickTool("selection");
      mouse.downAt(50, 80);
      mouse.moveTo(50, 130);
      mouse.moveTo(50, 180);
      mouse.upAt(50, 180);

      expect(getArrow().startBinding?.elementId).toBe("alice-rect");
      expect(getArrow().endBinding?.elementId).toBe("bob-rect");
    });
  });
});
```

## Step 2.5 done: selection and binding chokepoints

The typecheck and lint pass, and the full suite passes: 125 files, 1,860 tests. That's 5 new tests, with no new snapshot changes.

### What changed in the design

The hidden-element rule now also exists in **`@excalidraw/element`**, as two pure functions in `ownership.ts`. Element-level logic (selection, binding) can enforce it there, without the element package depending on the editor package. The editor's `visibility.ts` delegates to them, so the rule is still implemented in one place.

```
 @excalidraw/element                                    @excalidraw/excalidraw
 ownership.ts                                           scene/visibility.ts
  isElementByHiddenCreator(el, map, hiddenIds)  ◄────── isElementHiddenLocally  (delegates)
  excludeElementsByHiddenCreators(els, ids, map) ◄───── getLocallyVisibleElements (delegates)
        │                    │
        ▼                    ▼
 CHOKEPOINT 1: SELECTION     CHOKEPOINT 2: NEW BINDINGS
 groups.ts                   binding.ts  getBindingStrategyForDraggingBindingElementEndpoints
 selectGroupsForSelected…      ← bindOrUnbindBindingElement (arrow creation/finalize)
  ← click, box, lasso,         ← linearElementEditor (dragging an arrow endpoint)
    Select All, group,         ← App (pointer down/move)
    delete, deselect         arrows/focus.ts  handleFocusPointDrag (re-targeting a binding)
                             App.tsx  getBindableElements() → 8 suggestion/hover lookups

 deliberately NOT filtered:  binding.ts updateArrowBindings  → existing couplings survive
 backstop (unchanged):       App.componentDidUpdate selection safety net
```

**About `makeNextSelectedElementIds`:** I'd suggested it as the second chokepoint, but it only receives **IDs and the previous state, with no elements**, so it can't tell who made anything. It also has 34 callers, most of which select an element you just created. **Selection already has full coverage through `selectGroupsForSelectedElements`**, which Select All, clicks, box-select, lasso, and the group and delete actions all go through. So the second chokepoint went to **binding**, which is the interaction you described.

### Behaviour, as you specified it

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Draw a new arrow onto a hidden shape | It doesn't bind. Its end stays free, and the hidden shape's `boundElements` are unchanged |
| Hovering over a hidden shape with the arrow tool | No binding highlight |
| Drag an existing arrow's focus point onto a hidden shape | It doesn't re-target there |
| An arrow that was **already bound** to a shape before that shape was hidden | It **stays bound**. Moving the visible shape at the other end keeps both ends attached |
| Who sees what | Each element follows its own creator. A visible arrow bound to a hidden shape stays visible, and it still follows that shape when the hidden collaborator moves it. This is the "you can still see their changes" effect you described, and it's easy to change later |

### Files changed in step 2.5

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| [element/src/ownership.ts](packages/element/src/ownership.ts) | Added `isElementByHiddenCreator` and `excludeElementsByHiddenCreators` (returns the same array when nothing is hidden) |
| [element/src/groups.ts](packages/element/src/groups.ts) | **Chokepoint 1.** `selectGroupsForSelectedElements` drops hidden elements before expanding groups. `prevAppState` now requires `hiddenCollaboratorIds` in its type, and every existing caller already passes a full `AppState`, so no callers needed changes |
| [element/src/binding.ts](packages/element/src/binding.ts) | **Chokepoint 2.** The strategy dispatcher only considers visible bindable shapes. A comment explains why `updateArrowBindings` is left unfiltered |
| [element/src/arrows/focus.ts](packages/element/src/arrows/focus.ts) | The focus-point drag can't move a binding onto a hidden shape |
| [scene/visibility.ts](packages/excalidraw/scene/visibility.ts) | Now delegates to the element-package functions |
| [components/App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx) | Added `getBindableElements()`. The 8 `getHoveredElementForBinding` calls use it, and that's the only change to those lines (checked in the diff) |
| [tests/collaboratorVisibility.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorVisibility.test.tsx) | 5 new tests: the selection chokepoint called directly **with no App involved**, so it's tested on its own, plus a control; new arrow vs. hidden shape, plus a control; and an existing binding surviving a move |

### Checking it yourself

In a solo tab, with the console helpers: draw rectangles A and B, then `stamp("alice")` A and `stamp("bob")` B.

1. **New binding blocked:** run `hide("bob")`, then draw an arrow from A into the empty space where B is. Run `hide()`, and B reappears with the arrow **not** attached to it.
2. **Existing binding kept:** while both are visible, draw an arrow from A to B (it binds to both). Run `hide("bob")`, then drag A around. The arrow stays attached to A, and its other end stays where B is. Run `hide()`, and the arrow is still bound to B.
3. **Group selection:** group A and B, run `hide("bob")`, then click A. Only A is selected, with no group outline.

### Known limitations (documented, not fixed)

- **The elbow-arrow drag preview:** while you're dragging an **elbow** arrow, its route can briefly bend toward a hidden shape, because `getElbowArrowData` gets no state. It still won't bind there when you let go.
- **Arrow stacking order:** `moveArrowAboveBindable` can raise **your own** arrow above a hidden shape. That only changes your arrow, not the hidden shape.

Nothing is committed. `excalidraw-room` is untouched.

Type **"Approved"** to continue to step 3: client identity (the per-tab ID pool), the `USER_IDENTITY` message and automatic stamping.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 00:51:55Z)**_

There are **30 tests in two files**. I've grouped them by what they protect, with the code and a short note on what each one proves. At the end there's an honest list of what **isn't** covered, so you can judge whether the coverage is enough.

---

## File 1: [ownership.test.ts](packages/element/src/__tests__/ownership.test.ts) (5 unit tests)

These test `getElementCreatorId()` on its own, with no editor. That's the function every visibility decision depends on. Elements are built with the element package's own `newElement` and `newTextElement`, since ESLint doesn't allow this package to import the editor's test helpers.

```ts
const createRect = (creatorId?: unknown) =>
  newElement({
    type: "rectangle",
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    customData:
      creatorId === undefined ? undefined : { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId },
  });

const createLabel = (containerId: string, creatorId: string) =>
  newTextElement({
    text: "label",
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    containerId,
    customData: { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId },
  });
```

| Test | Proves |
| --- | --- |
| `returns the stamped creator id` | The normal case: `customData.creatorId = "alice"` gives `"alice"` |
| `returns UNKNOWN for elements without creator metadata` | Elements with no stamp (from older rooms) fall into the Unknown / Miscellaneous bucket |
| `returns UNKNOWN for malformed creator ids` | `""` and `42` don't become their own "collaborator". Bad data is treated as Unknown |
| `bound text follows its container's creator` | A label Bob typed inside Alice's shape counts as **Alice's**, so a label never shows or hides separately from its shape |
| `bound text falls back to its own stamp if container is missing` | If the container is missing, the text uses its own stamp, so a broken scene doesn't crash or misattribute |

```ts
it("bound text follows its container's creator", () => {
  const container = createRect("alice");
  const text = createLabel(container.id, "bob");
  expect(getElementCreatorId(text, arrayToMap([container, text]))).toBe(
    "alice",
  );
});
```

---

## File 2: [collaboratorVisibility.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorVisibility.test.tsx) (25 tests)

These render the real `<Excalidraw />` editor in jsdom.

### Shared helpers (top of the file)

```ts
// Stamp an element as if `creatorId` created it (stands in for step 3's automatic stamping)
const stamp = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(element: T, creatorId: string) =>
  newElementWith(element as ExcalidrawElement, {
    customData: { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId },
  }) as T;

// What the renderer would draw. jsdom's viewport is 0x0, which would cull
// everything, so pass an explicit 1000x1000 viewport (same trick as frame.test.tsx)
const getVisibleIds = () =>
  h.app.renderer
    .getRenderableElements({
      /* zoom, scroll…, */ height: 1000,
      width: 1000,
      hiddenCollaboratorIds: h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds /* … */,
    })
    .visibleElements.map((el) => el.id)
    .sort();

// Same as your console `hide(...)`, wrapped in act() so React finishes updating
const setHidden = (ids: string[]) => {
  act(() => {
    API.setAppState({ hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(ids) });
  });
};
```

**About the "(control)" tests:** several tests come in pairs. One runs with **nothing hidden** and shows the normal behaviour (for example, the eraser _does_ erase the whole group). The other runs with Bob hidden and shows the behaviour changes. Without the control, a test like "Bob wasn't erased" could pass just because the test's gesture missed every shape. That actually happened with box-select during this work, before I fixed the gesture.

### A. Rendering (8 tests), from step 1

Setup: Alice's rectangle, Bob's rectangle, and an **unstamped** "legacy" rectangle.

```ts
it("hides only the hidden collaborator's elements", () => {
  setHidden(["bob"]);
  expect(getVisibleIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect", "legacy-rect"]);
});

it("does not modify scene data when hiding", () => {
  const before = h.elements.map((el) => ({
    id: el.id,
    version: el.version,
    versionNonce: el.versionNonce,
    isDeleted: el.isDeleted,
  }));
  setHidden(["alice", "bob", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID]);
  expect(getVisibleIds()).toEqual([]);
  expect(h.elements.map(/* same fields */)).toEqual(before);
});
```

| Test | Proves |
| --- | --- |
| `renders everything by default` | The default is an empty set, so nothing is hidden |
| `hides only the hidden collaborator's elements` | Hiding Bob doesn't affect Alice or the legacy shape |
| `re-renders hidden elements when shown again` | Catches the **memo-key bug**: without the hidden set in the memo key, shapes wouldn't reappear |
| `hides untagged elements via the unknown bucket` | `"__unknown__"` hides only the legacy shape |
| `does not modify scene data when hiding` | **Shared-data integrity.** `version`, `versionNonce` and `isDeleted` are unchanged, and those are the fields that decide whether anything syncs to other clients |
| `bound text is hidden together with its container` | Hiding Bob hides his shape _and_ Alice's label inside it. Hiding Alice hides neither |
| `hides frame names (DOM) together with the frame` | The regression test for the frame-label bug you found, done by counting `.frame-name` DOM nodes |
| `is never persisted or exported` | `hiddenCollaboratorIds` is dropped from both the localStorage save and the export output of AppState |

### B. Interaction safety (8 tests), from step 2

Setup: solid-filled 100×100 rectangles, so clicking inside counts as a hit. Alice's is at x = 0 and Bob's at x = 200. Keyboard shortcuts are enabled.

```ts
it("select all + delete never deletes hidden elements", () => {
  setHidden(["bob"]);
  Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.A);
  });
  expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);

  Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.DELETE);
  expect(isDeleted("alice-rect")).toBe(true);
  expect(isDeleted("bob-rect")).toBe(false); // ← the core guarantee
});

const eraseThroughAliceRect = () => {
  UI.clickTool("eraser");
  mouse.downAt(-20, 50);
  mouse.moveTo(20, 50);
  mouse.moveTo(60, 50);
  mouse.upAt(60, 50);
};

it("(control) erasing a member erases the whole group", () => {
  eraseThroughAliceRect();
  expect(isDeleted("alice-rect")).toBe(true);
  expect(isDeleted("bob-rect")).toBe(true); // the eraser only touched Alice's shape…
});

it("erasing a visible member never erases hidden members", () => {
  setHidden(["bob"]);
  eraseThroughAliceRect();
  expect(isDeleted("alice-rect")).toBe(true);
  expect(isDeleted("bob-rect")).toBe(false); // …so this proves the fix
});
```

| Test | Proves |
| --- | --- |
| `clicking a hidden element doesn't select it` | Clicking where Bob's shape is selects nothing. Clicking Alice's still works |
| `(control) box-selecting selects all covered elements` | The drag gesture really does cover both shapes |
| `box-selecting skips hidden elements` | The same gesture with Bob hidden selects only Alice's shape |
| `select all + delete never deletes hidden elements` | **The scenario that most mattered**: Ctrl+A then Delete leaves Bob's shape alone |
| `hiding a selected element deselects it` | Selects both, hides Bob, and Bob's shape drops out of the selection (the `componentDidUpdate` safety net) |
| `selecting a visible member never selects hidden members` | In a mixed group, clicking Alice's shape selects only hers, with no group, and Delete leaves Bob's |
| `(control) erasing a member erases the whole group` | The eraser normally does expand to the whole group |
| `erasing a visible member never erases hidden members` | The eraser fix: that expansion skips hidden members |

### C. Export (4 tests), from step 2

```ts
const getExportedIds = (exportSelectionOnly = false) =>
  prepareElementsForExport(h.elements, h.state, exportSelectionOnly)
    .exportedElements.map((el) => el.id)
    .sort();

it("export follows the current visibility", () => {
  setHidden(["bob"]);
  expect(getExportedIds()).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);
  setHidden(["alice"]);
  expect(getExportedIds()).toEqual(["bob-rect"]);
});
```

| Test | Proves |
| --- | --- |
| `exports everything when nothing is hidden` | Nothing changes for users who don't use the feature |
| `exports only visible elements` | Hidden shapes are left out of image exports |
| `export follows the current visibility` | Your requirement that exports **reflect whatever is visible at that moment** |
| `getLocallyVisibleElements returns the same array when nothing is hidden` | A performance guarantee: with nothing hidden, you get **the same array back** (`toBe`, not `toEqual`), so no copying and no breaking memoization |

### D. Chokepoints (5 tests), from step 2.5

```ts
it("never returns hidden elements, even without the App safety net", () => {
  // Alice + Bob in one group, Bob hidden
  const result = selectGroupsForSelectedElements(
    {
      selectedElementIds: { "alice-rect": true, "bob-rect": true },
      editingGroupId: null,
    },
    h.app.scene.getNonDeletedElements(),
    h.state,
    null, // ← no App instance: tests the element-level chokepoint alone
  );
  expect(Object.keys(result.selectedElementIds)).toEqual(["alice-rect"]);
  expect(result.selectedGroupIds.group).toBeFalsy();
});

it("a new arrow can't bind to a hidden shape", () => {
  setHidden(["bob"]);
  drawArrowFromAliceToBob(); // arrow tool, drag from (50,50) into Bob's shape at (350,50)
  expect(getArrow().startBinding?.elementId).toBe("alice-rect");
  expect(getArrow().endBinding).toBeNull();
  expect(
    h.elements.find((el) => el.id === "bob-rect")!.boundElements ?? [],
  ).toEqual([]);
});

it("existing bindings to a hidden shape are kept", () => {
  drawArrowFromAliceToBob(); // bound to both while visible
  setHidden(["bob"]);
  UI.clickTool("selection");
  mouse.downAt(50, 80);
  mouse.moveTo(50, 130);
  mouse.moveTo(50, 180);
  mouse.upAt(50, 180); // drag Alice's shape
  expect(getArrow().startBinding?.elementId).toBe("alice-rect");
  expect(getArrow().endBinding?.elementId).toBe("bob-rect"); // still coupled
});
```

| Test | Proves |
| --- | --- |
| `never returns hidden elements, even without the App safety net` | Chokepoint 1 works **by itself**. Passing `app: null` rules out `componentDidUpdate`, so the element package's filter is what makes this pass |
| `(control) selects the whole group when nothing is hidden` | Normal group expansion still works through the same function |
| `(control) a new arrow binds to both shapes` | The arrow gesture really does reach Bob's shape and bind |
| `a new arrow can't bind to a hidden shape` | Chokepoint 2: the end stays free **and** Bob's `boundElements` are untouched, so his data never changes |
| `existing bindings to a hidden shape are kept` | Your "earlier couplings stay" rule: the arrow is still bound after the visible shape moves |

## What isn't covered

I'd rather you see these gaps than assume full coverage.

| Not directly tested | Current coverage | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isElementByHiddenCreator` / `excludeElementsByHiddenCreators` (the element-level helpers) | **Indirectly**, through every test above | Low. Small functions, heavily exercised |
| Embeddable and iframe hiding (`renderEmbeddables`) | Only your manual checks | Low-medium. Embeds need URL validation, so they're awkward to test in jsdom |
| JSON **Save / Save as** (`prepareDataForJSONExport`), the shareable link, and Excalidraw+ | Only image export is tested | **Medium**. Each is a one-line filter, but untested |
| Search menu (Ctrl+F) | None | Low-medium |
| Lasso selection | Only indirectly, since it goes through the tested selection chokepoint | Low |
| Text container pick, frame drop target, motion-path target | None | Low. Single filter conditions |
| Focus-point drag re-targeting (`arrows/focus.ts`) | None | Low-medium. Hard to simulate |
| The `selectedLinearElement` branch of the safety net | None | Low |
| **Moving the arrow itself** while one end is bound to a hidden shape | Only moving the _shape_ is tested | **Medium**. This is the edge case most likely to behave differently from what you expect |

```text
  saveCollabRoomToFirebase = async (
    syncableElements: readonly SyncableExcalidrawElement[],
  ) => {
    syncableElements = cloneJSON(syncableElements);
    try {
      const storedElements = await saveToFirebase(
        this.portal,
        syncableElements,
        this.excalidrawAPI.getAppState(),
      );

      this.resetErrorIndicator();

      if (this.isCollaborating() && storedElements) {
        this.handleRemoteSceneUpdate(this._reconcileElements(storedElements));
      }
    } catch (error: any) {
      const errorMessage = /is longer than.*?bytes/.test(error.message)
        ? t("errors.collabSaveFailed_sizeExceeded")
        : t("errors.collabSaveFailed");

      if (
        !this.state.dialogNotifiedErrors[errorMessage] ||
        !this.isCollaborating()
      ) {
        this.setErrorDialog(errorMessage);
        this.setState({
          dialogNotifiedErrors: {
            ...this.state.dialogNotifiedErrors,
            [errorMessage]: true,
          },
        });
      }

      if (this.isCollaborating()) {
        this.setErrorIndicator(errorMessage);
      }

      console.error(error);
    }
  };

  stopCollaboration = (keepRemoteState = true) => {
    this.queueBroadcastAllElements.cancel();
    this.queueSaveToFirebase.cancel();
    this.loadImageFiles.cancel();
    this.resetErrorIndicator(true);

    this.saveCollabRoomToFirebase(
      getSyncableElements(
        this.excalidrawAPI.getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted(),
      ),
    );

    if (this.portal.socket && this.fallbackInitializationHandler) {
      this.portal.socket.off(
        "connect_error",
        this.fallbackInitializationHandler,
      );
    }

    if (!keepRemoteState) {
      LocalData.fileStorage.reset();
      this.destroySocketClient();
    } else if (window.confirm(t("alerts.collabStopOverridePrompt"))) {
      // hack to ensure that we prefer we disregard any new browser state
      // that could have been saved in other tabs while we were collaborating
      resetBrowserStateVersions();

      window.history.pushState({}, APP_NAME, window.location.origin);
      this.destroySocketClient();

      LocalData.fileStorage.reset();

      const elements = this.excalidrawAPI
        .getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted()
        .map((element) => {
          if (isImageElement(element) && element.status === "saved") {
            return newElementWith(element, { status: "pending" });
          }
          return element;
        });

      this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
        elements,
        captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
      });
    }
  };

  private destroySocketClient = (opts?: { isUnload: boolean }) => {
    this.lastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion = -1;
    this.portal.close();
    this.fileManager.reset();
    if (!opts?.isUnload) {
      this.setIsCollaborating(false);
      this.setActiveRoomLink(null);
      this.collaborators = new Map();
      this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
        collaborators: this.collaborators,
      });
      LocalData.resumeSave("collaboration");
    }
  };

  private fetchImageFilesFromFirebase = async (opts: {
    elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[];
    /**
     * Indicates whether to fetch files that are errored or pending and older
     * than 10 seconds.
     *
     * Use this as a mechanism to fetch files which may be ok but for some
     * reason their status was not updated correctly.
     */
    forceFetchFiles?: boolean;
  }) => {
    const unfetchedImages = opts.elements
      .filter((element) => {
        return (
          isInitializedImageElement(element) &&
          !this.fileManager.isFileTracked(element.fileId) &&
          !element.isDeleted &&
          (opts.forceFetchFiles
            ? element.status !== "pending" ||
              Date.now() - element.updated > 10000
            : element.status === "saved")
        );
      })
      .map((element) => (element as InitializedExcalidrawImageElement).fileId);

    return await this.fileManager.getFiles(unfetchedImages);
  };

  private decryptPayload = async (
    iv: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>,
    encryptedData: ArrayBuffer,
    decryptionKey: string,
  ): Promise<ValueOf<SocketUpdateDataSource>> => {
    try {
      const decrypted = await decryptData(iv, encryptedData, decryptionKey);

      const decodedData = new TextDecoder("utf-8").decode(
        new Uint8Array(decrypted),
      );
      return JSON.parse(decodedData);
    } catch (error) {
      window.alert(t("alerts.decryptFailed"));
      console.error(error);
      return {
        type: WS_SUBTYPES.INVALID_RESPONSE,
      };
    }
  };

  private fallbackInitializationHandler: null | (() => any) = null;
```

```text
  startCollaboration = async (
    existingRoomLinkData: null | { roomId: string; roomKey: string },
  ) => {
    if (!this.state.username) {
      import("@excalidraw/random-username").then(({ getRandomUsername }) => {
        const username = getRandomUsername();
        this.setUsername(username);
      });
    }

    if (this.portal.socket) {
      return null;
    }

    let roomId;
    let roomKey;

    if (existingRoomLinkData) {
      ({ roomId, roomKey } = existingRoomLinkData);
    } else {
      ({ roomId, roomKey } = await generateCollaborationLinkData());
      window.history.pushState(
        {},
        APP_NAME,
        getCollaborationLink({ roomId, roomKey }),
      );
    }

    // TODO: `ImportedDataState` type here seems abused
    const scenePromise = resolvablePromise<
      | (ImportedDataState & { elements: readonly OrderedExcalidrawElement[] })
      | null
    >();

    this.setIsCollaborating(true);
    LocalData.pauseSave("collaboration");

    const { default: socketIOClient } = await import(
      /* webpackChunkName: "socketIoClient" */ "socket.io-client"
    );

    const fallbackInitializationHandler = () => {
      this.initializeRoom({
        roomLinkData: existingRoomLinkData,
        fetchScene: true,
      }).then((scene) => {
        scenePromise.resolve(scene);
      });
    };
    this.fallbackInitializationHandler = fallbackInitializationHandler;

    try {
      this.portal.socket = this.portal.open(
        socketIOClient(import.meta.env.VITE_APP_WS_SERVER_URL, {
          transports: ["websocket", "polling"],
        }),
        roomId,
        roomKey,
      );

      this.portal.socket.once("connect_error", fallbackInitializationHandler);
    } catch (error: any) {
      console.error(error);
      this.setErrorDialog(error.message);
      return null;
    }

    if (existingRoomLinkData) {
      // when joining existing room, don't merge it with current scene data
      this.excalidrawAPI.resetScene();
    } else {
      const elements = this.excalidrawAPI.getSceneElements().map((element) => {
        if (isImageElement(element) && element.status === "saved") {
          return newElementWith(element, { status: "pending" });
        }
        return element;
      });
      // remove deleted elements from elements array to ensure we don't
      // expose potentially sensitive user data in case user manually deletes
      // existing elements (or clears scene), which would otherwise be persisted
      // to database even if deleted before creating the room.
      this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
        elements,
        captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
      });

      this.saveCollabRoomToFirebase(getSyncableElements(elements));
    }

    // fallback in case you're not alone in the room but still don't receive
        this.portal.socket.off("first-in-room");
      }
      const sceneData = await this.initializeRoom({
        fetchScene: true,
        roomLinkData: existingRoomLinkData,
      });
      scenePromise.resolve(sceneData);
    });

    this.portal.socket.on(
      WS_EVENTS.USER_FOLLOW_ROOM_CHANGE,
      (followedBy: SocketId[]) => {
        this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
          appState: { followedBy: new Set(followedBy) },
        });

        this.relayVisibleSceneBounds({ force: true });
      },
    );

    this.initializeIdleDetector();

    this.setActiveRoomLink(window.location.href);

    return scenePromise;
  };

  private initializeRoom = async ({
    fetchScene,
    roomLinkData,
  }:
    | {
        fetchScene: true;
        roomLinkData: { roomId: string; roomKey: string } | null;
      }
    | { fetchScene: false; roomLinkData?: null }) => {
    clearTimeout(this.socketInitializationTimer!);
    if (this.portal.socket && this.fallbackInitializationHandler) {
      this.portal.socket.off(
        "connect_error",
        this.fallbackInitializationHandler,
      );
    }
    if (fetchScene && roomLinkData && this.portal.socket) {
      this.excalidrawAPI.resetScene();

      try {
        const elements = await loadFromFirebase(
          roomLinkData.roomId,
          roomLinkData.roomKey,
          this.portal.socket,
        );
        if (elements) {
          this.setLastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion(
            getSceneVersion(elements),
          );

          return {
            elements,
            scrollToContent: true,
          };
        }
      } catch (error: any) {
        // log the error and move on. other peers will sync us the scene.
        console.error(error);
      } finally {
        this.portal.socketInitialized = true;
      }
    } else {
      this.portal.socketInitialized = true;
    }
    return null;
  };
```

```text
  private initializeIdleDetector = () => {
    document.addEventListener(EVENT.POINTER_MOVE, this.onPointerMove);

  setCollaborators(sockets: SocketId[]) {
    const collaborators: InstanceType<typeof Collab>["collaborators"] =
      new Map();
    for (const socketId of sockets) {
      collaborators.set(
        socketId,
        Object.assign({}, this.collaborators.get(socketId), {
          isCurrentUser: socketId === this.portal.socket?.id,
        }),
      );
    }
    this.collaborators = collaborators;
    this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({ collaborators });
  }

  updateCollaborator = (socketId: SocketId, updates: Partial<Collaborator>) => {
    const collaborators = new Map(this.collaborators);
    const user: Mutable<Collaborator> = Object.assign(
      {},
      collaborators.get(socketId),
      updates,
      {
        isCurrentUser: socketId === this.portal.socket?.id,
      },
    );
    collaborators.set(socketId, user);
    this.collaborators = collaborators;

    this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
      collaborators,
    });
  };

  public setLastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion = (version: number) => {
    this.lastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion = version;
  };

  public getLastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion = () => {
    return this.lastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion;
  };

  public getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted = () => {
    return this.excalidrawAPI.getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted();
  };

  onPointerUpdate = throttle(
    (payload: {
      pointer: SocketUpdateDataSource["MOUSE_LOCATION"]["payload"]["pointer"];
      button: SocketUpdateDataSource["MOUSE_LOCATION"]["payload"]["button"];
      pointersMap: Gesture["pointers"];
    }) => {
      payload.pointersMap.size < 2 &&
        this.portal.socket &&
        this.portal.broadcastMouseLocation(payload);
    },
    CURSOR_SYNC_TIMEOUT,
  );

  relayVisibleSceneBounds = (props?: { force: boolean }) => {
    const appState = this.excalidrawAPI.getAppState();

    if (this.portal.socket && (appState.followedBy.size > 0 || props?.force)) {
      this.portal.broadcastVisibleSceneBounds(
        {
          sceneBounds: getVisibleSceneBounds(appState),
        },
        `follow@${this.portal.socket.id}`,
      );
    }
  };

  onIdleStateChange = (userState: UserIdleState) => {
    this.portal.broadcastIdleChange(userState);
  };

  broadcastElements = (elements: readonly OrderedExcalidrawElement[]) => {
    if (
      getSceneVersion(elements) >
      this.getLastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion()
    ) {
      this.portal.broadcastScene(WS_SUBTYPES.UPDATE, elements, false);
      this.lastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion = getSceneVersion(elements);
      this.queueBroadcastAllElements();
    }
  };

  syncElements = (elements: readonly OrderedExcalidrawElement[]) => {
    this.broadcastElements(elements);
    this.queueSaveToFirebase();

      WS_SUBTYPES.UPDATE,
      this.excalidrawAPI.getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted(),
      true,

    const currentVersion = this.getLastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion();
    const newVersion = Math.max(
      currentVersion,
      getSceneVersion(this.getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted()),
    );
    this.setLastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion(newVersion);
```

```typescript
/**
 * Per-tab collaborator identity.
 *
 * Every open tab is its own collaborator (matching the per-tab cursors and
 * avatars), yet a closed tab's id can be reclaimed later so its drawings stay
 * attributed to it:
 *
 * - the browser profile keeps a pool of ids in localStorage
 * - a tab claims an id by holding a Web Lock named after it for its lifetime
 *   (the browser releases it when the tab closes or crashes)
 * - a tab prefers the id in its own sessionStorage (reloads, restored tabs);
 *   a duplicated tab copies sessionStorage but can't get that lock, so it
 *   falls through to a free/new id
 *
 * Without Web Locks we fall back to sessionStorage only (per-tab, but a
 * closed tab's id is not reclaimed).
 */

import { randomId } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { STORAGE_KEYS } from "../app_constants";

/** cap so the pool can't grow unbounded over time */
const MAX_POOL_SIZE = 32;
const POOL_LOCK_NAME = "excalidraw-client-id-pool";
const getIdLockName = (id: string) => `excalidraw-client-id:${id}`;

const readPool = (): string[] => {
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(
      localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEYS.LOCAL_STORAGE_CLIENT_IDS) || "[]",
    );
    return Array.isArray(parsed)
      ? parsed.filter((id): id is string => typeof id === "string" && !!id)
      : [];
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
};

const writePool = (pool: string[]) => {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(
      STORAGE_KEYS.LOCAL_STORAGE_CLIENT_IDS,
      JSON.stringify(pool.slice(-MAX_POOL_SIZE)),
    );
  } catch {
    // storage unavailable (private mode, quota…) — id stays tab-local
  }
};

const readSessionId = (): string | null => {
  try {
    return sessionStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEYS.SESSION_STORAGE_CLIENT_ID);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
};

const writeSessionId = (id: string) => {
  try {
    sessionStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.SESSION_STORAGE_CLIENT_ID, id);
  } catch {
    // storage unavailable — id is still valid for this page lifetime
  }
};

/**
 * Resolves `true` once this tab holds the id's lock, `false` if another tab
 * holds it. A held lock is kept until the tab closes.
 */
const tryClaimId = (locks: LockManager, id: string): Promise<boolean> =>
  new Promise((resolve) => {
    locks
      .request(getIdLockName(id), { ifAvailable: true }, (lock) => {
        if (!lock) {
          resolve(false);
          return;
        }
        resolve(true);
        // never settles → lock is held for the lifetime of the tab
        return new Promise<never>(() => {});
      })
      .catch(() => resolve(false));
  });

const claimIdFromPool = (locks: LockManager): Promise<string> =>
  // serialize pool access across tabs so two tabs opened at once don't
  // overwrite each other's additions
  locks.request(POOL_LOCK_NAME, async () => {
    const pool = readPool();
    const sessionId = readSessionId();
    const candidates = sessionId
      ? [sessionId, ...pool.filter((id) => id !== sessionId)]
      : pool;

    for (const id of candidates) {
      if (await tryClaimId(locks, id)) {
        if (!pool.includes(id)) {
          writePool([...pool, id]);
        }
        return id;
      }
    }

    const id = randomId();
    await tryClaimId(locks, id);
    writePool([...pool, id]);
    return id;
  });

const acquireClientId = async (): Promise<string> => {
  const locks = typeof navigator !== "undefined" ? navigator.locks : undefined;

  let id: string | null = null;
  if (locks) {
    try {
      id = await claimIdFromPool(locks);
    } catch (error: any) {
      console.error("Failed to claim collaborator id from pool", error);
    }
  }

  id = id ?? readSessionId() ?? randomId();
  writeSessionId(id);
  return id;
};

let clientIdPromise: Promise<string> | null = null;

/** This tab's collaborator id. Stable for the tab's lifetime. */
export const getClientId = (): Promise<string> => {
  if (!clientIdPromise) {
    clientIdPromise = acquireClientId();
  }
  return clientIdPromise;
};
```

```typescript
import { CREATOR_ID_KEY } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

/**
 * Elements this client introduced to the room that don't carry its creator
 * stamp yet: newly drawn, pasted or duplicated (new id, possibly with a
 * copied foreign stamp), or restored by undo/redo without the stamp.
 *
 * Elements first received from other clients are never (re)stamped, so edits
 * never transfer ownership.
 *
 * @param remoteElementIds ids of elements that first reached this client from
 * the room (other clients or the room's stored scene)
 */
export const getElementsToStamp = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  remoteElementIds: ReadonlySet<string>,
  clientId: string,
): T[] =>
  elements.filter(
    (element) =>
      !element.isDeleted &&
      !remoteElementIds.has(element.id) &&
      element.customData?.[CREATOR_ID_KEY] !== clientId,
  );

export const getStampedCustomData = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  clientId: string,
): NonNullable<ExcalidrawElement["customData"]> => ({
  ...element.customData,
  [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: clientId,
});
```

```text
        roomId ?? this.roomId,
        encryptedBuffer,
        iv,
      );
```

```text
describe("collaboration", () => {
  it("should emit two ephemeral increments even though updates get batched", async () => {
    const durableIncrements: DurableIncrement[] = [];
    const ephemeralIncrements: EphemeralIncrement[] = [];

    await render(<ExcalidrawApp />);

    h.store.onStoreIncrementEmitter.on((increment) => {
      if (StoreIncrement.isDurable(increment)) {
        durableIncrements.push(increment);
      } else {
        ephemeralIncrements.push(increment);
      }
    });

    // eslint-disable-next-line dot-notation
    expect(h.store["scheduledMicroActions"].length).toBe(0);
    expect(durableIncrements.length).toBe(0);
```

```typescript
import { CREATOR_ID_KEY, newElementWith } from "@excalidraw/element";
import { API } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/tests/helpers/api";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import {
  getElementsToStamp,
  getStampedCustomData,
} from "../collab/creatorStamp";

const ME = "me";

const createRect = (id: string, creatorId?: string) =>
  newElementWith(API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", id }), {
    customData: creatorId ? { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId } : undefined,
  }) as ExcalidrawElement;

const getIdsToStamp = (
  elements: ExcalidrawElement[],
  remoteIds: string[] = [],
) => getElementsToStamp(elements, new Set(remoteIds), ME).map((el) => el.id);

describe("getElementsToStamp", () => {
  it("stamps elements this client introduced", () => {
    expect(getIdsToStamp([createRect("new")])).toEqual(["new"]);
  });

  it("never stamps elements received from the room (edits don't transfer ownership)", () => {
    expect(getIdsToStamp([createRect("theirs", "alice")], ["theirs"])).toEqual(
      [],
    );
    // untagged legacy elements stay untagged (→ Miscellaneous)
    expect(getIdsToStamp([createRect("legacy")], ["legacy"])).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("restamps pasted/duplicated copies of someone else's element", () => {
    // new id (not remote) carrying the original's copied stamp
    expect(getIdsToStamp([createRect("pasted", "alice")])).toEqual(["pasted"]);
  });

  it("skips elements already stamped by this client", () => {
    expect(getIdsToStamp([createRect("mine", ME)])).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("skips deleted elements", () => {
    const deleted = newElementWith(createRect("deleted"), { isDeleted: true });
    expect(getIdsToStamp([deleted])).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("getStampedCustomData", () => {
  it("sets the creator while keeping other customData", () => {
    const element = newElementWith(API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" }), {
      customData: { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: "alice", other: 1 },
    });

    expect(getStampedCustomData(element, ME)).toEqual({
      [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: ME,
      other: 1,
    });
  });
});
```
